name: libpng
notes: Requires zlib installed into PORT_PREFIX first.
The first successful CRT configure run required vfprintf, sprintf, vsprintf, inttypes.h, strings.h, strtoimax, strtoumax, bzero, and bcmp.

libpng's configure is real GNU Autoconf output (unlike zlib's hand-written script), so it runs config.guess, which does not recognize plain Windows `uname` output (`uname -s = Windows`, no MSYS/Cygwin/MinGW userland) and fails with 'unable to guess system type'. --build=aarch64-w64-mingw32 works around this on Windows aarch64; this is currently hardcoded to that one architecture and will need to become x86_64-w64-mingw32 (or be made dynamic) to also cover Windows x86_64.

Same -U_WIN32/-U__WIN32__/etc. CFLAGS trick as zlib.json, plus -U__NT__ (pngpriv.h's own Windows guard also checks __NT__): without it, pngpriv.h's `#if defined(_WIN32) || defined(__WIN32__) || defined(__NT__) / #include <windows.h>` fires -- this project's sysroot has no real Windows SDK <windows.h> (its own Win32 API surface is declared privately inside libc/src/arch/windows/, not exposed publicly) -- and configure fails outright with 'windows.h file not found'. Nothing near that include in pngpriv.h/png.c/pngerror.c actually references a real Windows API symbol from it, so undefining the trigger macros (keeping libpng on its generic/POSIX code paths, matching what this project's CRT actually provides) is correct, not just a workaround -- same reasoning as zlib.json's own note.
